subject: Re: On-prem bundle — amortization examples & migration credit options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orthomed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem bundle options & amortization examples

Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture two pragmatic packaging routes you can model for Orthomed's on-prem (VPC) deployment: a pilot-first amortization and a 12‑month blended commit. Both try to balance your CAPEX timing and the need for an ops retainer.

Attached is a quick worksheet (Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Q2v3.xlsx) with line items broken into: operator licenses, platform fee (monthly), implementation SOW, and optional 24/7 on-call. Two quick notes:
- Pilot amortization: we can spread the platform fee across 12 months and apply a 50% platform fee credit for the pilot period (first 3 months) if you commit to a 12‑month conversion.
- Blended commit: a 12‑month upfront commit that reduces operator license unit price by 15% and provides a one‑time migration credit (applied to first invoice) for data egress/import costs.

What would be most helpful from you: a high-level expected peak GPUs and whether a single site or multi‑site topology (HA across two sites) — that changes the operator license count and the SRE retainer.

I copied Marissa for implementation SOW timing. If you want, we can turn this into a short mutual action plan and circulate to procurement.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Q2v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Foster <afoster@orthomed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orthomed.com>
Date: 2026-04-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem bundle options & amortization examples

Vanessa —

Thanks for the breakdown. Helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:
1) We are aiming for an initial pilot to cover our flagship data center only (single-site). Peak expected load ~ 8 A100-equivalents.
2) Budget posture: capital-constrained for FY26 Q3; procurement prefers amortization or credits applied to first-year invoices rather than large upfront platform fees.
3) Migration credit: any documentation on what Redwood will cover vs what we need to budget for (network egress, engineer hours)?

Also, one procurement constraint: we need to understand whether the platform fee is capitalizable (we prefer to treat operator licenses as CapEx but platform fees as OpEx) — any guidance helps with our finance approvers.

If you can propose 2 line-item scenarios we can show to our CFO, that would speed things up.

Best,
Alex Foster
Head of Platform Engineering
Orthomed Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orthomed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem bundle options & amortization examples

Alex — quick reply and I've looped in Irene (legal/procurement support) and Marissa (SOW/implementation).

High level responses to your bullets:
- Single-site with ~8 GPUs: we'll recommended operator license for 10 units to cover headroom, and a standard 2‑week cutover SOW for the pilot.
- Platform fee capitalization: Redwood's platform fee is typically treated as a subscription (OpEx). However, we can structure the commercial terms so the customer pays the platform fee via a 12‑month invoice schedule which sometimes meets capital accounting needs; we can't reclassify it contractually as a license but the payment terms are flexible. Recommend you confirm with your finance team.
- Migration credit: Redwood offers a one‑time migration credit applied to first invoice. It can cover network egress up to an agreed cap and a modest number of professional services hours (we typically size 40–80 hours for this class of pilot). Anything beyond that is billed per the SOW.

Proposal: I'll ask Marissa to draft two succinct scenarios in the spreadsheet: (A) 3-month pilot with 50% pilot platform fee credit + conversion to 12-month amortization; (B) 12-month blended commit with 15% operator license discount + $30k migration credit.

Next step: Marissa — can you push the two scenarios into the workbook and add a one‑page SOW appendix we can reference in procurement?

Thanks —
Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Foster <afoster@orthomed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem bundle options & amortization examples

Alex / Vanessa —

I've updated the attached workbook with two packaged scenarios and added a one‑page SOW appendix (OnPrem_SOW_Template_v1.2.pdf) that lists deliverables, estimated PS hours, and milestone schedule. Summary:

Scenario A — Pilot-first amortization- Operator licenses: 10 units- Platform fee: amortized monthly over 12 months; pilot months (months 0–2) receive 50% platform fee credit- Migration credit: $20,000 (covers network egress cap + 40 PS hrs)- Implementation timeline: 6–8 weeks to pilot (cutover + validation)

Scenario B — 12-month blended commit- Operator licenses: 10 units with 15% unit discount- Platform fee: standard monthly invoicing (no pilot credit) but $30,000 migration credit applied to invoice 1- Implementation timeline: 4–6 weeks (faster turnaround with committed engineering slots)

I've also added a short table showing invoice timing and amortization examples for finance to review.

Attachment: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Q2v3.xlsx (updated)
Attachment: OnPrem_SOW_Template_v1.2.pdf (SOW appendix)

Irene — if you can confirm any legal constraints around the migration credit language and a simple cancellation clause for pilot conversion, we can prepare a procurement-friendly redline.

—Marissa
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orthomed.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem bundle options & amortization examples

Alex —

Quick legal note on the mechanics:
- Migration credit: we'll include a line in the order form describing the dollar cap and eligible items (network egress, up to X engineering hours to support data import). Any overage billed at standard PS rates; we'll provide an invoice credit equal to the agreed cap and list excluded items (third-party managed services, hardware replacement).
- Pilot conversion: propose a 30‑day conversion window after pilot completion. If Orthomed converts within that window, the remaining platform fee balance is amortized over the contractual term per the chosen scenario.
- Termination for convenience: 60 days with pro‑rated refunds on pre-paid operator license fees only; platform fee prepayments are non-refundable if used.

I'll prepare a short procurement addendum and send a DocuSign link once we confirm scenario choice. If you want the pilot to include a 50% platform fee credit + $20k migration credit, we can lock that in for a 3-month pilot.

I can circulate a DocuSign powerform (sample link below) and a clean order form once you confirm the package.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
